subject: agriculture
topicTitle: Care and Management of Cattle, Poultry, Dairy Technology, Animal Nutrition
thirtySecondSummary: Livestock production provides drought resistance, milk, meat, eggs, and organic manures, forming the backbone of Indian mixed farming systems.

Indigenous cattle breeds (Bos indicus) possess a prominent hump, dewlap, and heat tolerance (Milch: Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Gir; Draught: Amritmahal, Hallikar; Dual: Hariana, Tharparkar, Ongole); Exotic breeds (Bos taurus) include Holstein-Friesian and Jersey.
Buffalo breeds (Bubalus bubalis) contribute over 50% of India's milk production; Murrah is the premier dairy breed ('Black Gold'), alongside Nili-Ravi, Mehsana, and Jaffarabadi.

Animal nutrition differentiates Roughages (crude fiber > 18%, TDN < 60%) from Concentrates (crude fiber < 18%, TDN > 60%); Silage (anaerobic preservation of green fodder, lactic acid pH 3.8-4.2) and Hay making preserve seasonal surplus.

Dairy technology covers milk composition (Colostrum, casein, lactose), legal standards (Cow milk: 3.5% Fat, 8.5% SNF; Buffalo milk: 6.0% Fat, 9.0% SNF), Pasteurization (LTLT: 63°C for 30 min; HTST: 72°C for 15 sec), and common livestock diseases (Foot & Mouth Disease, Anthrax, Ranikhet).

coreConcepts.title: Classification of Cattle and Buffalo Breeds
coreConcepts.explanation:
Indian indigenous cattle belong to Bos indicus (humped, Zebu cattle), known for heat tolerance, disease resistance, and tick tolerance.
1. Milch Breeds: Cows produce high milk yields, bullocks poor for draught.
- Sahiwal: Origin Montgomery (Pakistan); sweetest milk, loose skin ('Lola'), reddish-dun color.
- Gir: Origin Kathiawar (Gujarat); convex forehead, pendulous leaf-like curled ears.
- Red Sindhi: Origin Karachi; deep red body.
2. Draught Breeds: Bullocks excellent for plowing and carting, cows poor milkers (Amritmahal, Hallikar, Nagori, Khillari).
3. Dual Purpose Breeds: Cows good milkers, bullocks good for draft (Hariana, Tharparkar, Ongole, Kankrej - known for 'Sawai Chaal').
4. Exotic Breeds: Holstein-Friesian (highest milk yield in the world, black and white patches), Jersey (highest fat percentage among exotics, 5-5.5%).
5. Buffalo Breeds: Murrah (jet black, tightly curled horns like spiral rings, world's highest dairy yielder); Mehsana (cross of Murrah x Surti); Surti (sickle-shaped horns); Bhadawari (copper-colored body, highest milk fat up to 13%).
keyTakeaways: Sahiwal: Best indigenous dairy cow, loose skin (Lola).
Gir: Pendulous leaf-like curled ears, convex forehead.
Murrah: Premier buffalo, tightly curved spiral horns, jet black.
Bhadawari: Highest fat percentage in buffalo milk (up to 13%).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: ICAR Class XII Unit II, Cattle & Buffalo breeds, pp. 50-62.

coreConcepts.title: Feeds, Animal Nutrition, and Fodder Preservation
coreConcepts.explanation:
Ruminant digestion relies on rumen microbial fermentation of fibrous feedstuffs.
1. Feed Classification:
- Roughages: Bulky feeds with > 18% crude fiber (CF) and < 60% Total Digestible Nutrients (TDN). Green roughages: Legumes (Berseem, Lucerne, Cowpea) rich in protein and calcium; Non-legumes (Maize, Jowar, Bajra, Napier grass). Dry roughages: Straw, Stover, Hay.
- Concentrates: Low fiber (< 18% CF), high energy/protein (> 60% TDN). Energy-rich: Maize, wheat, barley, rice bran; Protein-rich: Mustard cake, groundnut cake, cotton seed cake, soybean meal.
2. Fodder Preservation:
- Silage: Green fodder preserved under anaerobic conditions by controlled lactic acid fermentation in silos. Best crops: Carbohydrate-rich fodders like Maize, Sorghum, Bajra. Quality silage has pH 3.8-4.2, greenish-yellow color, and sweet aroma (lactic acid > acetic acid).
- Hay: Fodder dried to < 15% moisture to prevent spoilage without losing nutrients. Best crop for hay: Thin-stemmed legumes like Oat and Lucerne.
keyTakeaways: Roughages: CF > 18%, TDN < 60%; Concentrates: CF < 18%, TDN > 60%.
Silage: Anaerobic fermentation of maize/jowar; ideal pH 3.8 - 4.2.
Hay: Moisture content reduced to below 15%; ideal crop is Oat / Lucerne.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: ICAR Class XII Unit II, Feeds & Nutrition section, pp. 64-75.

coreConcepts.title: Dairy Technology, Milk Standards & Poultry Management
coreConcepts.explanation:
1. Milk Constituents & Colostrum: Colostrum is the first secretion post-parturition rich in immunoglobulins (antibodies), protein, and minerals. Milk protein is Casein (80%); sugar is Lactose; principal mineral is Calcium.
2. Legal Standards (PFA / FSSAI):
- Cow Milk: Minimum 3.5% Milk Fat, 8.5% Solids-Not-Fat (SNF).
- Buffalo Milk: Minimum 6.0% Milk Fat, 9.0% SNF.
- Standardized Milk: 4.5% Fat, 8.5% SNF.
- Toned Milk: 3.0% Fat, 8.5% SNF.
- Double Toned Milk: 1.5% Fat, 9.0% SNF.
3. Pasteurization Methods: Destroys pathogenic microbes (especially Mycobacterium tuberculosis & Coxiella burnetii).
- Low Temperature Long Time (LTLT): 63°C (145°F) for 30 minutes.
- High Temperature Short Time (HTST): 72°C (161°F) for 15 seconds.
- Ultra High Temperature (UHT): 135-150°C for 1-2 seconds.
4. Poultry Systems & Diseases: Deep litter vs Cage system; Broilers (meat, 6-7 weeks) vs Layers (egg production starting at 20 weeks). Diseases: Ranikhet / Newcastle disease (viral, respiratory distress, twisting neck), Marek's disease (paralysis), Coccidiosis (protozoan, bloody diarrhea treated with amprolium).
keyTakeaways: Cow milk standard: 3.5% Fat, 8.5% SNF; Buffalo milk: 6.0% Fat, 9.0% SNF.
Pasteurization: LTLT (63°C for 30 min) vs HTST (72°C for 15 sec).
Ranikhet (Newcastle) disease: Highly contagious viral infection of poultry.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: ICAR Class XII Unit II, Dairy & Poultry section, pp. 78-91.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Origin: Rohtak, Hisar (Haryana) | Characteristics: Jet black body, tightly coiled spiral horns
keyFacts.explanation: Known as 'Black Gold' of India; highest milk yielding buffalo breed averaging 2000-2500 kg per lactation.
keyFacts.examTip: CUET asks which breed is called Black Gold of Haryana.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: 72°C (161°F) for exactly 15 seconds, followed by rapid cooling to < 4°C
keyFacts.explanation: Destroys all vegetative pathogens without imparting cooked flavor or damaging milk vitamins.
keyFacts.examTip: Phosphatase test confirms complete pasteurization efficiency.

keyFacts.explanation: Prepared by blending whole buffalo milk with skimmed milk powder and water.
keyFacts.examTip: Double toned milk is 1.5% Fat and 9.0% SNF.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Paramyxovirus-1 | Acute viral disease of poultry
keyFacts.explanation: Characterized by gasping, torticollis (twisted neck), greenish watery diarrhea, and 100% mortality in unvaccinated flocks.
keyFacts.examTip: Vaccination: F1 strain at 1-7 days; R2B / Mukteswar strain at 6-8 weeks.

workedExamples.question: According to statutory legal standards in India, what are the minimum prescribed Milk Fat and Solids-Not-Fat (SNF) percentages for cow milk?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Recall the standard milk legal compositions under FSSAI / PFA regulations.
Step 2: Cow milk requires a minimum of 3.5% Fat and 8.5% SNF.
Step 3: (Buffalo milk requires 6.0% Fat & 9.0% SNF; Toned milk requires 3.0% Fat & 8.5% SNF).
workedExamples.cuetInsight: Questions testing legal fat and SNF percentages across cow, buffalo, and toned milk are guaranteed points in the dairy section.

workedExamples.question: Which buffalo breed is famous for having the highest fat percentage (up to 13%) in its milk, accompanied by a distinct copper-colored body coat?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Look at the identifying traits: 'copper colored body' and 'highest milk fat (up to 13%)'.
Step 2: Bhadawari breed, originating from the Agra and Etawah region of Uttar Pradesh, possesses these exact characteristics.
Step 3: (Murrah is jet black with coiled horns; Surti has sickle horns).
workedExamples.cuetInsight: Unique breed signatures (Bhadawari copper coat, Gir curled ears, Kankrej sawai chaal) are standard CUET stems.

commonTraps.whyItTraps: Silage requires carbohydrate-rich green fodder preserved anaerobically with 60-70% moisture; Hay requires thin-stemmed green fodder dried down to < 15% moisture.
commonTraps.howToAvoid: Silage = Wet & Anaerobic (pH 3.8-4.2); Hay = Dry (< 15% moisture).

commonTraps.trap: Confusing HTST and LTLT temperature-time combinations.
commonTraps.whyItTraps: LTLT is 63°C for 30 minutes; HTST is 72°C for 15 SECONDS (not 15 minutes!).
commonTraps.howToAvoid: Note the units: HTST is 15 seconds.

keyPoints: Milch Cattle: Sahiwal (Lola, sweetest milk), Gir (pendulous ears), Red Sindhi.
Draught: Amritmahal, Hallikar, Nagori; Dual: Hariana, Tharparkar, Kankrej.
Buffaloes: Murrah ('Black Gold', spiral horns); Bhadawari (copper coat, up to 13% fat); Surti (sickle horns).

Milk Legal Standards: Cow = 3.5% Fat, 8.5% SNF; Buffalo = 6.0% Fat, 9.0% SNF; Toned = 3.0% Fat, 8.5% SNF.

practiceQuestions.question: Which buffalo breed of Haryana is universally celebrated as the 'Black Gold' due to its exceptional milk yield?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Murrah buffaloes, originating from Rohtak, Hisar, and Jind districts of Haryana, are termed 'Black Gold' due to their superior genetics and milk production.

practiceQuestions.question: Under the High Temperature Short Time (HTST) pasteurization method, milk is heated to which temperature for what duration?
practiceQuestions.explanation: HTST pasteurization involves heating milk to 72°C (161°F) for 15 seconds in continuous plate heat exchangers, followed by rapid chilling to under 4°C.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following is categorized as a leguminous green fodder exceptionally rich in protein and calcium?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Berseem (Egyptian clover) is a prime leguminous rabi green fodder containing 18-20% crude protein and high calcium content.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): Maize is considered the most ideal crop for silage making.
Reason (R): Maize stalks contain an abundant concentration of fermentable water-soluble carbohydrates that facilitate rapid lactic acid production under anaerobic conditions.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Both statements are correct and (R) explains why maize produces superior quality silage with a stable low pH (3.8-4.2).

practiceQuestions.question:
Match List-I (Cattle Breed) with List-II (Category):
List-I:
(P) Sahiwal
(Q) Amritmahal
(R) Hariana
(S) Holstein-Friesian

List-II:
(1) Exotic Dairy Breed
(2) Indigenous Draught Breed
(3) Indigenous Milch Breed
(4) Dual Purpose Breed
practiceQuestions.explanation: Sahiwal = Indigenous Milch; Amritmahal = Indigenous Draught; Hariana = Dual Purpose; Holstein-Friesian = Exotic Dairy.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the maximum permissible moisture percentage in good quality 'Hay' to prevent microbial molding and spontaneous heating during storage?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Hay must be dried until moisture drops below 15% (ideally 12-14%) to inhibit bacterial and fungal spoilage in storage stacks.

practiceQuestions.question: Toned milk is manufactured by standardizing whole buffalo milk to which legal specifications?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Toned milk has statutory limits of minimum 3.0% Fat and 8.5% Solids-Not-Fat (SNF).

practiceQuestions.question: The contagious poultry disease characterized by gasping, green diarrhea, and twisting of the neck (torticollis) caused by a Paramyxovirus is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Ranikhet (Newcastle) disease is caused by Avian Paramyxovirus-1, producing acute respiratory, digestive, and nervous signs.

practiceQuestions.question: Which test is routinely employed in dairy processing laboratories to verify the completeness and efficiency of milk pasteurization?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The alkaline phosphatase enzyme naturally present in raw milk is slightly more heat-resistant than pathogens; its total inactivation indicates adequate pasteurization.

practiceQuestions.question: Colostrum fed to newborn calves within the first few hours of birth is critical because it contains high concentrations of:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Calves are born without protective maternal antibodies; colostrum delivers pre-formed immunoglobulins across the gut mucosa to confer passive immunity against infections.
